chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: My father (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not marry off the rest of his daughters, nor did he marry any of his wives for more than twelve Owqiya and one Nash; the Owqiya is forty [Dirhams], and the Nash is twenty [Dirhams].

key_terms.أُوقِيَّة: A unit of weight/currency, defined here as 40 Dirhams
key_terms.دِرْهَماً: Dirham, a silver coin and unit of currency
key_terms.نَشّ: A smaller unit of currency, defined here as 20 Dirhams

ai.seo_question: What was the maximum dowry given to the Prophet's wives according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a prophetic precedent for modesty in dowries (mahr), specifying that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) did not exceed twelve Owqiya and one Nash for his wives. This narration is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the Sunnah of marriage, emphasizing that excessive dowries are contrary to the Prophet's practice and promoting financial ease for the community. The specific valuation of these ancient currency units provides scholars with a benchmark for understanding the economic context of early Islamic marriages.
